content_voiceover: This slide distinguishes double hit from double expresser lymphoma, a common point of confusion on boards. Double hit lymphoma is a genetic diagnosis, defined by concurrent rearrangement of M-Y-C together with B-C-L-two, or less commonly B-C-L-six, detected by fluorescence in situ hybridization, F-I-S-H. These rearrangements cluster mostly within the germinal center B cell subtype. Double expresser lymphoma, by contrast, is a protein level, immunohistochemistry based diagnosis, defined simply by high expression of both M-Y-C and B-C-L-two proteins, regardless of whether the underlying gene rearrangements are present, and it can occur in either germinal center or activated B cell subtypes. Prognostically these are distinct: in the referenced cohort, classical diffuse large B cell lymphoma without either feature had the best overall survival, roughly sixty percent at long term follow up; double expresser lymphoma had intermediate outcomes; and double hit lymphoma had the worst outcomes, with survival curves separating early and significantly, p less than zero point zero zero one for double hit versus classical, and p equals zero point zero one four for double expresser versus classical. Reflecting this biology, the WHO twenty twenty two classification renamed double hit as diffuse large B cell lymphoma or high grade B cell lymphoma with M-Y-C and B-C-L-two rearrangements, while the I-C-C twenty twenty two classification calls it high grade B cell lymphoma with M-Y-C and B-C-L-two rearrangements.
keypoints: Double hit lymphoma: concurrent MYC plus BCL2 (or BCL6) rearrangement, confirmed by FISH
Double expresser lymphoma: high MYC and BCL2 protein by IHC, without requiring gene rearrangement
Outcome ranking: classical DLBCL best, double expresser intermediate, double hit worst (P<.001, P=.014)
WHO 2022 and ICC 2022 both reclassify double hit as high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements
keypoint_voiceover: Do not confuse these two entities. Double hit is a genetic, F-I-S-H based diagnosis, M-Y-C plus B-C-L-two rearrangement, and carries the worst prognosis. Double expresser is a protein, immunohistochemistry based diagnosis, high M-Y-C and B-C-L-two expression without necessarily having the rearrangement, and it carries an intermediate prognosis, worse than classical D-L-B-C-L but better than double hit. Both the WHO and I-C-C twenty twenty two classifications now formally recognize double hit as its own high grade B cell lymphoma category.
